# Thematic Portfolio v2 — Market-Section Diversification Design Spec

## 1. Current system summary

The thematic book is picked and sized by a purely per-ticker additive scorer: `_merge_signals` ranks names by `count × source_weight` and truncates to top-25 (`thematic_auto.py:1376`), `_ai_pick` asks a free LLM for the "TOP 6 highest-conviction LONG plays" with no diversification instruction (`:1633`), and the `for pick in picks:` loop (`:3791`) is the single chokepoint that creates pending signals. Diversification is an afterthought bolted on at approval time — a `PORTFOLIO_MAX_PER_THEME=3` count cap keyed off a noisy LLM theme label (`:2444`, `:5835`) and a 30% GICS dollar cap that lives only in the sizer, runs only on the adaptive path, and **fails open to `math.inf`** on any missing sector (`position_sizer.py:242`). Because ~7 of the 12 themes are the same AI/semiconductor macro trade, the book can be 12 positions of one factor and never trip a single cap.

## 2. Top concentration gaps

- **Fake-diverse taxonomy.** ~7 of 12 themes (ai_leaders, ai_infrastructure, optical_network, memory_hbm, datacenter_power, quantum_future, nuclear_energy) are one AI/semis macro bet; `PORTFOLIO_MAX_PER_THEME=3` (`thematic_auto.py:2444`) permits 3+3+3+3 = 12 correlated AI names.
- **Zero sector awareness at pick time.** `_merge_signals` sorts and truncates with no grouping (`:1376`); `composite_score` is a per-ticker scalar blind to the rest of the book (`:2570`); the `_ai_pick` prompt has no diversification objective (`:1633`).
- **The one real cross-theme dollar cap fails open.** `_portfolio_aware_dollar` runs sector/close/ADV enrichment under a single 12s `asyncio.wait_for`; on timeout `sectors={}` (`thematic_auto.py:4373`) → `sector_room = math.inf` (`position_sizer.py:242`) — the cap silently vanishes exactly for the small/illiquid names most prone to cluster.
- **Wrong granularity.** GICS is orthogonal to the risk: the AI trade spans Technology, Utilities (datacenter power/nuclear), Materials (critical minerals) and Comm Services, so a 100% AI-supply-chain book passes every per-GICS 30% check.
- **Sector never persisted.** Positions store the constant `"sector":"thematic"` (`:5859`), forcing a full yfinance re-derivation of the whole book on every approval.
- **Live leg bypasses caps.** The Fidelity block (`:5892`) runs outside/after the paper lock, never reads `cap_reason`, and `_size_fidelity_position` re-clamps only to 10% + cash (`fidelity.py:1925`) — a paper position blocked for concentration still places the real order.
- **Scoring actively amplifies concentration.** `thematic_portfolio.py:204-207` scores premium AI themes at 9.0 vs 5.5 for everything else.
- **Policy layer is concentration-seeking by design.** `portfolio_policy.evaluate` optimizes "concentration in the best ideas" with zero sector/theme dimension (`portfolio_policy.py:18`, `:212`).
- **Weak/off correlation defenses.** `_correlation_guard_for_book` is default-OFF (`thematic_auto.py:5261`); the sizer `correlation_factor` is a soft, single-worst-pairwise shrink needing the same fragile 12s price load (`position_sizer.py:161`).

## 3. RECOMMENDED core mechanism

**Adopt the MACRO-CLUSTER BUDGET + DRIFT TILT method (research digest "construction"), with the correlation layer as an optional soft backstop only.**

The primitive is a static, network-free `_THEME_MACRO` fold that collapses the 12 narrative themes into ~6 macro-clusters (all AI sub-themes → `ai_complex`), derived from the `theme` string **every signal and position already carries**. Each cluster gets a hard **names count cap**, a hard **dollar budget** (% of account), and a **soft geometric size-decay tilt** so the hot narrative can still be the largest bucket (first two names full conviction, up to 35%) but every marginal name adds less. GICS sector is kept as an orthogonal cross-check, hardened to **fail-closed** (unknown sector → its own singleton bucket, never `math.inf`).

**Why this over the alternatives:**
- **vs. risk-parity / ERC (rejected):** needs a covariance matrix from 6mo closes loaded inside the exact 12s window that already fails open; noisy/ill-conditioned on a 10-20 name book; the solver output is opaque on a HIL card ("why is my size $312?"); and — fatally — ERC on GICS still calls a 100%-AI-supply-chain book "balanced."
- **vs. capacity/ADV allocation:** orthogonal, not a substitute — it bounds single-name liquidity and is already the `liquidity_adv` limit (`position_sizer.py:254`). Keep it; it doesn't spread the book across sections.
- **vs. pure correlation clustering:** 60d correlation on hot momentum names is noisy and spikes toward 1.0 in every selloff (procyclical — it would over-block precisely in a drawdown). Correct as a **soft shrink + N_eff advisory**, wrong as the hard floor. The macro-theme layer is the stable floor; correlation is the confirmation for when the LLM mislabels a name.

The decisive win: the cluster label is network-free, so the primary cap **keeps biting exactly when the data pipeline is degraded** — the opposite of the current GICS cap. It matches the repo's pure/sync/network-free rule-engine pattern (holdings_brain / portfolio_policy / position_sizer) and plugs into hooks the code map already identified — a bounded additive change, not a rewrite.

## 5. Implementation plan (ordered)

1. **`_THEME_MACRO` map + `_macro_cluster(theme, sector=None)`** next to `THEMES_MAP` (`thematic_auto.py:1417`), env-overridable via `THEMATIC_CLUSTER_MAP`. Ship this first — every later step reads it. Include the `_GICS_TO_MACRO` fallback so real Fidelity holdings without a theme still get a cluster.
2. **New pure module `tradingagents/portfolio/diversification.py`** — `DiversifyConfig.from_env()`, `_bucket_key` (fail-closed), `diversification_room(...)` returning `(dollar_cap, decay_mult, reason)`. Pure list/dict arithmetic, fully unit-testable in isolation. Land with its tests before any wiring.
3. **Persist buckets** (`thematic_auto.py:5859`): store real `sector` + `macro_cluster` on the position dict. This makes the book's buckets readable cheaply and unblocks the caps.
4. **Sizer wiring** (`position_sizer.py`): add `cluster` field to `SizingCandidate`/`BookPosition`, multiply `raw` by `decay`, append `("cluster_cap", cluster_room)` to the `min()` limits, and flip the `:242` unknown→`math.inf` branch to the fail-closed singleton bucket. Dollar-truthful home for the hard budget.
5. **`_portfolio_aware_dollar` injection** (`:4322-4392`): set candidate + each `BookPosition` `cluster=_macro_cluster(theme)` from the already-stored `theme` (pure dict read, survives the 12s timeout). Feed the real book, not just paper, once GICS fallback is in.
6. **Pick-time count backstop** (`for pick in picks:` loop, `:3791`): seed cluster/sector tallies from the unified book, `continue` on the hard count cap before append. This is the "don't even propose the 4th AI name" rule and the only one covering the non-sizer branches.
7. **Approve-time backstop** (`:5827-5838`): cluster count + cluster/sector dollar cap in the cap ladder, setting `cap_reason`.
8. **Live-leg parity** (`:5892`, `fidelity.py:1925`): honor `cap_reason` / re-run `diversification_room` against the unified real+paper book before placing the real order. **This is the correctness-critical step — "propose-only diversification" is a lie for real money until this lands.** Never weaken `validate_live_order`, step-up 2FA, or the compliance kill-chain — this is an *additional* gate, subtractive of orders only.
9. **Rank-time interleave** (`:1376`) + **prompt nudge** (`:1633`): pre-diversify the LLM shortlist. Soft, free.
10. **De-bias scoring** (`thematic_portfolio.py:204-207`): remove the premium-AI 9.0 boost.
11. **(Optional, later) correlation soft backstop**: summed-corr load + N_eff advisory; flip `THEMATIC_CORRELATION_GUARD` on. Keep as soft shrink/advisory only — hard blocks stay on the stable theme layer.

Staged rollout: ship steps 1-3 dark, then enable `DIVERSIFY_ENABLED` with soft tilt only, then turn on hard count/dollar caps, then `DIVERSIFY_ENFORCE_LIVE`.

## 6. Tests needed

**Pure module (`test_diversification.py`, no network):**
- `_macro_cluster`: all 12 themes fold to the expected macro bucket; unknown/`future_tech` → catch-all; JSON env override reassigns nuclear/quantum; GICS→macro fallback for a theme-less real holding.
- `diversification_room`: hard names cap returns `(0.0, 0.0, reason)` at the Nth name; dollar budget clamps `cap` to remaining room; soft decay sequence is exactly `1.0, 1.0, 0.6, 0.36, ...`; **fail-closed** — unknown GICS sector becomes its own singleton bucket (never `math.inf`, never a false block).
- Structural guarantee: with count cap C and `MAX_POSITIONS=N`, a full book always spans ≥ `ceil(N/C)` clusters.

**Sizer (`test_position_sizer.py`):**
- `cluster_cap` appears in the `min()` limits and binds when it is smallest; `binding_constraint` reports `cluster_cap`.
- `:242` regression: unknown sector no longer yields `math.inf` — cap remains active.
- Decay multiplier composes with existing `f_conv × f_q × f_vol × f_corr` without altering them when cluster is empty (1.0x).
- Name shrunk below `SIZER_MIN_DOLLAR` is naturally skipped.

**Integration (mock scan / approve, network-free stubs):**
- Monolithic AI ranked list → pick loop creates ≤ N `ai_complex` pendings; rank interleave spreads the top-20.
- Approve ladder sets `cap_reason` on the (N+1)th same-cluster signal; `force=true` bypasses (HIL authority preserved).
- **Live-leg parity: a paper position blocked by a diversification cap does NOT place a Fidelity order** (the current documented gap) — assert the order call is not made.
- Fail-open discipline: with sector enrichment timed out (`sectors={}`), the cluster cap (from `theme`) still binds; only the GICS cross-check degrades to per-ticker singletons.
- Compliance regression: `validate_live_order`, step-up 2FA, 10%/$50k/limit-only gates unchanged; diversification only ever removes/shrinks orders.

**Existing suite:** must stay green (currently 1377); add ~25-35 tests.

## 7. Open questions for the user

1. **Cluster count cap value.** `DIVERSIFY_MAX_NAMES_PER_CLUSTER=4` on a 10-name book guarantees ≥3 clusters; setting it to 3 guarantees ≥4. Do you want a harder floor (3) at the cost of cutting the hot narrative sooner?
2. **Cluster dollar budget.** 35% per macro-cluster still lets AI be the biggest bucket by far. Too loose (you want ≤25%?) or about right for a momentum book?
3. **Nuclear / quantum / critical-minerals membership.** These are the judgment calls — should `nuclear_energy`, `quantum_future`, and `critical_minerals` fold into `ai_complex` (they're mostly AI-datacenter/chip-supply plays) or stay standalone? This one mapping decision is the whole lever.
4. **Live-leg enforcement stance.** Enforce diversification caps on real Fidelity orders from day one (`DIVERSIFY_ENFORCE_LIVE=true`), or paper-only first and add live parity after you've watched the paper book behave?
5. **Real-book contribution.** Should a Fidelity account already heavy in `ai_complex` throttle new same-cluster *paper* picks too (unified book), or keep paper and real cluster budgets separate?
6. **Correlation layer.** Ship the optional statistical backstop (Layer 2/3, effort L) in v2, or defer it and rely on the theme-macro floor + hardened GICS cross-check for the first release?
7. **Scoring de-bias.** Just remove the premium-AI 9.0 boost, or actively invert it into a diversification bonus for under-represented clusters (a stronger, more opinionated tilt)?

## Appendix A — System map (agent findings)

### Thematic SIGNAL→PICK pipeline (scan → merge/rank → AI pick → pending-signal creation) in web/api/thematic_auto.py

**Flow:** One `_run_scan()` cycle (thematic_auto.py:3538, under `_scan_lock`) drives everything: (1) fan out ~19 scrapers via `asyncio.gather` (reddit, ddg, yahoo, google_news, seeking_alpha, stockanalysis, marketaux, insider, trusted_twitter, stocktwits, finviz, rss, av_movers, yahoo_movers, brave, google_trends, discovery, analyst, options_flow), each timeout-bounded, each returning {ticker: count} or [tickers]. (2) `_merge_signals()` (:1138) is the ranker: for every source it does `scores[ticker] += count × source_weight`, capping each source's per-ticker contribution at `_MAX_PER_SOURCE_PTS` so breadth beats one viral feed; then layers on a multi-source confirmation bonus (+3 per quality source, max +15), a scan-memory historical bonus, sentiment-weighted buzz modulation (buzz_score.compute_buzz), an insider+social combo (+8), a quality gate (drop low-signal-only names unless score≥80), a single-source ×0.7 dampener, AI ticker validation, and yfinance validation. It returns `ranked = sorted(scores, desc)[:25]` — a flat per-ticker score list, plus a per-source breakdown. (3) `_ai_pick(ranked, news_blobs)` (:1682) sends the top-20 ranked tickers + DDG news headlines to a free LLM (Cloudflare llama-3.3-70b → OpenRouter fallback) with `_build_ai_pick_prompt` (:1633) asking for the 'TOP 6 highest-conviction LONG plays'; `_sanitize_picks` (:1573) clamps every field to guardrails and folds the LLM's theme string to a canonical THEMES_MAP key via `_canonical_theme`. (4) Back in `_run_scan`, the `for pick in picks:` loop (:3791) is the single chokepoint that creates pending signals: per pick it `continue`s on already-owned (`_existing_portfolio` incl. brain-held), already-pending, avoid-flag (net social selling), not-in-policy-top-N, then clamps conviction, computes `_comp = composite_score(conviction, raw_score, sentiment)` (:3843), applies a price-confirmation multiplier, and gates on `MIN_COMPOSITE_SCORE` (:3860, default 70, env THEMATIC_MIN_SIGNAL_SCORE). Survivors get appended as `status:"pending"` dicts carrying a `theme` field. `portfolio_policy.evaluate` (:3780) reconciles picks against the unified real+paper book and caps output to top-N actionable (capacity/manage-first, NOT sector-aware). Pending signals then go to HIL `approve_signal` (:5529), which is the first place any theme/sector cap actually bites.

**Sector awareness:** At the moment of PICKING (ranking + pending-signal creation) there is effectively ZERO sector/theme awareness — selection is pure per-ticker additive score. `_merge_signals` ranks and truncates to top-25 with no grouping by sector or theme; `composite_score` (:2570) is a per-ticker conviction×buzz×sentiment scalar that never sees the rest of the book; the `_ai_pick` prompt (:1633) literally says 'Pick the TOP 6 highest-conviction' with no diversification instruction, so if AI/semis is the hot narrative the LLM returns 6 semis names. Each pick does carry a `theme` label (one of 12 THEMES_MAP keys, assigned by the LLM or `_guess_theme`), but that label is never used during the scan to limit how many picks share a theme or sector. Theme/sector only enters at APPROVAL time in `approve_signal`: (a) `PORTFOLIO_MAX_PER_THEME = 3` (:2444) blocks the 4th open position with the same *thematic theme label* (`theme_count`, :5830) — counting only the thematic paper book; (b) `position_sizer.size_position` applies a `max_sector_pct` = 30% dollar cap by real GICS sector (`_sector_of`, :4242), but it fails OPEN to `math.inf` (position_sizer.py:242) whenever the sector is unknown or the 12s enrichment times out; (c) `_correlation_guard_for_book` adds a price-correlation cap (not a sector count). So the only genuine cross-theme sector guard is a best-effort dollar cap evaluated per-signal after the human is already looking at the card — never a 'don't pick the 4th name from the same sector' rule at pick time.

**Concentration risks:**
- THEMES_MAP taxonomy is fake diversification: ~7 of the 12 themes (ai_leaders, ai_infrastructure, optical_network, memory_hbm, datacenter_power, quantum_future, plus nuclear_energy as AI-power) are the SAME macro AI/semiconductor complex and mostly GICS Technology/Comm-Services. PORTFOLIO_MAX_PER_THEME=3 therefore permits 3+3+3+3 = 12 positions all riding one AI factor, each labelled a 'different theme'.
- The picker ranks purely by buzz/momentum score, and buzz clusters by narrative — when AI/semis is trending, the entire ranked[:25], the top-20 fed to the LLM, and all 6 AI picks are one sector. Nothing in _merge_signals or the pick loop rebalances or interleaves by sector.
- The one real cross-theme guard (position_sizer 30% GICS dollar cap) fails OPEN to math.inf when _sector_of returns None or the 12s enrich times out (position_sizer.py:242) — precisely for the small-cap/illiquid names most prone to cluster, so the cap silently vanishes exactly when concentration is worst.
- That sector dollar cap only sees the thematic PAPER book (PAPER_STATE_FILE positions), not the real Fidelity holdings — real-book sector concentration doesn't stop a new same-sector paper pick, and it's dollar-weighted (30% of account) not a count cap, so many small same-sector names slip under it.
- No count-based 'Nth name per sector/theme' rule exists anywhere at pick time — the loop's `seen` set only dedupes exact tickers (:3793), and `_TICKER_ALIASES` only folds dual-class lines; two different semis names never trip any counter.
- The _ai_pick prompt gives the LLM no diversification objective and no view of the current book, so its 'top 6 highest-conviction' will happily be monolithic; the deterministic sanitizer downstream also has no sector logic.
- PORTFOLIO_MAX_PER_THEME keys off the LLM-assigned/`_guess_theme` label, which is noisy and defaults to 'future_tech' — mislabels either over-block or leak concentration past the theme counter.

**Diversification hooks:**
- PRIMARY: the `for pick in picks:` loop in _run_scan (thematic_auto.py:3791-3898) — the single chokepoint every new pending signal passes. It already computes `_comp`, holds `pick['theme']`, maintains `seen`/`created_this_scan`, and already `continue`s on several skip conditions just before appending (near the MIN_COMPOSITE_SCORE gate at :3860). A running sector/theme tally — seeded from open `_existing_portfolio` + carried `_already_pending`, incremented per created signal — plus a `continue` when a bucket hits N is the natural home for 'don't create the 4th same-sector pending'. `_sector_of(t)` (:4242, cached) resolves GICS and `pick['theme']` is the cheap theme key.
- `_merge_signals` final ranking (thematic_auto.py:1376, `sorted(scores)[:25]`) — re-rank/interleave to demote the Nth same-sector name before the LLM ever sees it, so `_ai_pick` receives an already-diversified shortlist. Sector lookup on ~25 cached names is cheap (batchable like `_closes_map`).
- `_build_ai_pick_prompt` (thematic_auto.py:1633) — add an explicit 'diversify across themes/sectors, at most N names per theme' instruction to the LLM prompt. Soft (model-obeyed) but free; pairs with a hard downstream cap.
- `portfolio_policy.evaluate` (called thematic_auto.py:3780; module tradingagents/portfolio/portfolio_policy.py) — already the top-N actionable selector that reconciles against the unified real+paper book; the correct place for a portfolio-level 'sector budget' constraint once `_pol.Candidate` is given a sector field.
- The approval cap ladder in approve_signal (thematic_auto.py:5832-5838) — extend the existing `PORTFOLIO_MAX_PER_THEME` chain with a GICS-sector COUNT cap and/or a macro-cluster cap; backstop only (approval-time, per-signal).
- `position_sizer.size_position` sector cap (tradingagents/portfolio/position_sizer.py:234-242) — already computes sector_room; hardening it to fail CLOSED and feeding it the REAL book plus a macro-bucket (not raw GICS) would make the existing dollar guard actually bite.
- MISSING PRIMITIVE to add: a theme→macro-bucket map (e.g. `_THEME_MACRO = {ai_leaders:'ai_semis', ai_infrastructure:'ai_semis', optical_network:'ai_semis', memory_hbm:'ai_semis', datacenter_power:'ai_semis', quantum_future:'ai_semis', ...}`) sitting next to THEMES_MAP (:1417) and `_THEME_ALIASES` (:1498) — this collapse is the cheap lever that converts the currently-useless per-theme cap into a real concentration cap for whichever hook consumes it.

### Thematic sizing → approval → execution (the dollar-allocation + concentration-cap surface)

**Flow:** DOLLAR ALLOCATION PER NAME is a 4-branch decision tree in approve_signal (thematic_auto.py:5587-5619), picked in order:
(1) explicit body.dollar_amount OR conviction_scale=OFF → policy_alloc = flat base_dollar (default $500), NO caps applied here.
(2) DEFAULT PATH (adaptive_sizing=True + conviction_scale=True + thematic paper-book value>0) → await _portfolio_aware_dollar (thematic_auto.py:4322) which calls the whole-book sizer size_position (position_sizer.py:190). This is the ONLY branch that applies the sector/heat/correlation/cash hard caps. If portfolio context can't be built it falls back to _adaptive_dollar (10%-only clamp); if the sizer returns $0 (a cap bound it to <min_dollar) approve raises 400 'No portfolio room' unless force=true.
(3) scan-stamped size_factor>0 → base_dollar × size_factor (size_factor = conviction × how-full-the-book-is, portfolio_policy.py:182 — NO sector/theme dimension).
(4) else → _conviction_dollar(base_dollar, conviction) (thematic_auto.py:4121) — 0.4×–1.5× conviction scale, NO caps.

The sizer (size_position) computes raw = account × base_pct(4%) × conviction × quality × inverse_vol × correlation, then takes the MIN of hard limits: per_position_cap(10%), sector_room(30%−already-in-sector), portfolio_heat(80%−deployed), liquidity_adv(1% ADV), cash. Smallest binding limit wins (position_sizer.py:249-257).

TWO WRITE LEGS run from the single policy_alloc:
- PAPER leg (thematic_auto.py:5815-5890, inside _paper_state_lock): re-checks PORTFOLIO_MAX_POSITIONS(10-20), PORTFOLIO_MAX_PER_THEME(3, COUNT), PORTFOLIO_MAX_SPECULATIVE(8), _correlation_guard_for_book (default OFF), _check_portfolio_circuit_breakers (heat 80% + daily-loss + settled cash). If any bind → cap_reason set → paper position skipped. Note: NO per-position 10% clamp is re-applied here, so branches 1/3/4 rely on base_dollar being small.
- LIVE FIDELITY leg (thematic_auto.py:5892-5933, OUTSIDE the paper lock, AFTER it): fires whenever fidelity_trade+execute_fidelity+live flags are on. It passes live_alloc=policy_alloc into _size_fidelity_position (fidelity.py:1925), which re-clamps ONLY to 10% single-name cap + available cash. It does NOT read cap_reason, so a paper position blocked by the theme-count / heat / correlation / circuit-breaker caps STILL places the real order. Real money is gated only by compliance.validate_live_order (10%, $50k, limit-only, trusted quote) + step-up 2FA + the 10%/cash re-clamp.

**Sector awareness:** Real GICS sector IS used, but narrowly and fragilely. _sector_of (thematic_auto.py:4242) resolves a ticker's GICS sector from yfinance .info['sector'], falls back to a free-AI classifier (_ai_sector_fill, 4225) into the 11 GICS buckets, and persists to sector_cache.json. _portfolio_aware_dollar (4346-4373) fetches sectors for the candidate AND every book ticker, then hands them to size_position, whose sector_room math (position_sizer.py:234-242) enforces the 30% cap.

Enforcement gaps: (a) the whole enrichment (sectors + 6mo closes + ADV for candidate and every holding) runs under a single 12s asyncio.wait_for; on timeout/exception sectors={} (thematic_auto.py:4373) → candidate.sector=None → sector_room=math.inf (position_sizer.py:242) → the 30% cap SILENTLY DISABLES (fail-open). yfinance .info is exactly the slow/rate-limited call most likely to blow the budget. (b) The 30% cap lives ONLY in the sizer (branch 2); the explicit-dollar, size_factor, and _conviction_dollar branches carry ZERO sector awareness. (c) The LIVE Fidelity leg has NO sector concept at all. (d) portfolio_policy.evaluate (the pick-time discipline layer) has NO sector/theme dimension — purely capacity + conviction (its stated goal, portfolio_policy.py:18, is 'concentration in the best ideas'). (e) Stored paper positions set sector='thematic' literal (thematic_auto.py:5859), so any downstream groupby on the position's own sector field is meaningless — the real GICS sector is re-derived live each approve and never persisted.

Crucially, GICS is the WRONG granularity for this book's concentration problem: the AI trade spans Technology (NVDA/AVGO), Utilities (datacenter-power VST/CEG, nuclear), Materials (critical minerals), and Communication Services — so a portfolio that is 100% a single AI-supply-chain macro bet sits comfortably under every per-GICS-sector 30% cap.

**Concentration risks:**
- The only true market-section DOLLAR cap is the sizer's 30% GICS-sector limit (position_sizer.py:240), and it FAILS OPEN: _portfolio_aware_dollar's 12s enrichment timeout or any yfinance/AI hiccup → sectors={} (thematic_auto.py:4373) → sector_room=inf → cap silently off. It is also absent on the explicit-dollar, size_factor, and _conviction_dollar branches (thematic_auto.py:5587-5619).
- GICS sector is orthogonal to the actual risk: the AI/semiconductor cluster is spread across Technology, Utilities (datacenter power + nuclear), Materials (critical minerals), and Comm Services, so a book that is entirely one AI-derivative bet passes all per-GICS-sector 30% checks. There is NO theme/cluster dollar cap tying these together.
- Per-theme control is COUNT-ONLY (PORTFOLIO_MAX_PER_THEME=3 names, thematic_auto.py:2444) and DEFAULT_THEMES is dominated by AI-adjacent buckets (ai_leaders, ai_infrastructure, memory_hbm, optical_network, datacenter_power, nuclear_energy, quantum). 3 names × ~7 AI themes far exceeds any dollar discipline; only PORTFOLIO_MAX_SPECULATIVE=8 and MAX_POSITIONS(10-20) bound the count, and NO per-theme dollar cap exists.
- The LIVE Fidelity leg is the LEAST diversified path: _size_fidelity_position (fidelity.py:1925) enforces only the 10% single-name cap + available cash — no sector, no theme, no heat, no correlation. And the Fidelity block (thematic_auto.py:5892) runs outside/after the paper-state lock and never checks cap_reason, so real orders fire even when the paper leg's theme-count/heat/correlation/circuit-breaker caps blocked the paper position.
- Correlation defenses are weak or off: the hard guard _correlation_guard_for_book is DEFAULT-OFF (THEMATIC_CORRELATION_GUARD=false, thematic_auto.py:5261) and only on the paper leg; the sizer's correlation_factor (position_sizer.py:161) is a soft shrink capped at -50% and only fires when 6mo closes load inside the same fragile 12s window.
- The pick-time policy portfolio_policy.evaluate (portfolio_policy.py:212) — the deterministic 'safety floor' that decides which candidates even become signals — has zero sector/theme awareness; it optimizes for concentration in the highest-conviction ideas, actively working against the v2 diversification goal.
- Per-position 10% cap is NOT re-applied on the paper write for branches 1/3/4 (only the sizer and _adaptive_dollar clamp to 10%); with defaults ($500 base on a $100k paper book) this is negligible, but a user-set large dollar_amount with conviction_scale off has no per-name clamp on the paper leg.

**Diversification hooks:**
- SizerConfig (position_sizer.py:69) already carries max_sector_pct=30 and size_position (249-257) already selects the smallest of a list of named hard limits — adding a 'theme_cap'/'cluster_cap' limit is a one-line addition to that limits list plus one groupby, and SizerConfig.from_env (85) makes it env-tunable.
- SizingCandidate/BookPosition (position_sizer.py:45-66) already carry a per-name sector; adding a parallel 'theme' or 'cluster' field lets the sizer aggregate an AI-supply-chain bucket independent of GICS. _portfolio_aware_dollar (thematic_auto.py:4375-4388) is the single place that builds these objects with real per-name weights + cash, so it is the natural injection point — but its 12s fail-OPEN must become fail-closed (or use a pre-warmed sector/theme cache) for any new cap to be trustworthy.
- Every signal and paper position already carries a `theme` (DEFAULT_THEMES key) and the per-theme COUNT is already computed at approve time (thematic_auto.py:5830) — turning that into a per-theme DOLLAR aggregation/cap is a minimal extension right where the count cap already lives.
- _sector_of + _SECTOR_CACHE (thematic_auto.py:4242) is a ready-made cached, AI-backfilled per-ticker classifier; it can emit a coarser 'macro cluster' label (e.g. AI-infrastructure) alongside GICS so the cap operates at the granularity the concentration problem actually lives at.
- _check_portfolio_circuit_breakers (thematic_auto.py:5417) already iterates all positions computing portfolio heat — a per-sector/per-theme heat computation attaches here, and if this gate were moved to also cover the live leg it would close the real-money diversification gap.
- portfolio_policy.evaluate/PolicyConfig (portfolio_policy.py:212) already has a suppress_generation mechanism and env-driven config (from_env) — a per-theme/cluster quota could stop over-concentrated candidates from ever becoming signals, upstream of sizing.
- The live-leg gap needs its own fix point: _size_fidelity_position (fidelity.py:1925) or the approve Fidelity block (thematic_auto.py:5892) is where a real-money sector/theme cap must be enforced, since the paper-side caps demonstrably do not gate the live order.

### Book shape: position/theme caps, portfolio-manager policy, mechanical exits, and concentration logic for the thematic (social-momentum) system

**Flow:** Two layers shape the book. (1) At SCAN time, portfolio_policy.evaluate() (tradingagents/portfolio/portfolio_policy.py:212) runs a strict "manage-first" hierarchy against the unified book (real Fidelity holdings + open thematic positions, merged at thematic_auto.py:3710 via _brain_held_tickers): hard-cap 20 -> manage only; if any "strong" position (conv>=6, constructive status, target_progress<0.8) is still progressing and no candidate is "clearly superior" -> SUPPRESS new-signal generation this cycle; at capacity (>=10) only a clearly-superior candidate (conv >= weakest+2 AND higher expected return) may REPLACE the weakest; near-capacity (>=8/10) new entries need conv>=8; else open NEW; if full with no superior idea -> ADD to the highest-conviction holding. It returns at most top_n=3 actions and stamps a size_factor onto each signal. The module docstring (line 18) states the explicit goal is "risk-adjusted return through concentration in the best ideas, not trade count" — the policy is concentration-SEEKING by design. (2) At APPROVE time (thematic_auto.py:5529 approve_signal), three hard COUNT caps gate every new entry (lines 5827-5838): PORTFOLIO_MAX_POSITIONS (default 10, env THEMATIC_MAX_POSITIONS clamped 10-20; .env=10), PORTFOLIO_MAX_PER_THEME=3, PORTFOLIO_MAX_SPECULATIVE=8, plus an optional (default-OFF) correlation guard (line 5841). Sizing then runs through _portfolio_aware_dollar (thematic_auto.py:4322) -> position_sizer.size_position. Exits are a separate, purely per-position mechanical scan, _check_thematic_exits (thematic_auto.py:2985): stop_hit, target_hit (-> switch to trailing stop to let winners run), max_hold (green runners -> trailing instead of dump), and buzz_collapse/buzz_decay (only on flat/red names, with an AI news gate). holdings_brain assesses each REAL holding independently (hold/trim/add/exit/adopt) and only trims a single name over its conviction-adjusted % ceiling. So the book holds ~10 names (hard 20), shaped by conviction-ranked concentration into the best ideas — nothing spreads it.

**Sector awareness:** Sector awareness is thin, soft, and split across two different notions of "sector." (A) THEME buckets: every thematic position is stamped sector:"thematic" plus a narrative theme (thematic_auto.py:5859-5859). PORTFOLIO_MAX_PER_THEME=3 (thematic_auto.py:2444) caps names per THEME, counted at line 5830 by matching sig theme. But themes are narrative, not GICS: the taxonomy (_THEME_ALIASES thematic_auto.py:1498-1512; valid themes at 1674) SPLITS the single AI/semiconductor/datacenter macro trade into ~5 separate themes — ai_leaders, ai_infrastructure (semis/GPU), optical_network, memory_hbm, datacenter_power — so ~10 highly-correlated AI-capex names spread across those themes NEVER trip the 3-per-theme cap. (B) GICS sector DOLLAR cap: position_sizer.SizerConfig.max_sector_pct=30.0 (position_sizer.py:73, env SIZER_MAX_SECTOR_PCT) caps dollar weight in one real GICS sector at 30% of account (sector_room computed position_sizer.py:234-240, applied as one of the min() limits at 257). Real GICS sector is resolved by _sector_of / _ai_sector_fill (thematic_auto.py:4242-4260, cached) and injected for both candidate and book in _portfolio_aware_dollar (4375-4388). BUT it is a DOLLAR cap not a name count, it only throttles/blocks the marginal NEW buy (never trims or rebalances), it is FAIL-OPEN (sector fetch has a 12s timeout; on failure sector->None-> sector_room=inf, no clamp, position_sizer.py:242), and it only runs on the adaptive path (acct_val>0). There is NO cap on names-per-sector anywhere, and NOTHING rebalances toward a target sector/theme spread — exits and holdings_brain are strictly per-position.

**Concentration risks:**
- dup-key placeholder — see the populated concentration_risks array above

**Diversification hooks:**
- PORTFOLIO_MAX_PER_THEME cap check (thematic_auto.py:2444 def; enforced 5830+5835) — the existing count-cap seam; a parallel PORTFOLIO_MAX_PER_SECTOR count cap using _sector_of(ticker) can attach right here
- position_sizer limits list + sector_room (position_sizer.py:234-257) — add a names-per-sector count constraint to the min() limits, or make the 30% dollar cap fail-CLOSED instead of inf-on-missing
- _sector_of / _ai_sector_fill (thematic_auto.py:4242-4260) — GICS sector resolution for any ticker already exists and is cached; the classification infra a sector-spread rule needs is already built
- _canonical_theme + _THEME_ALIASES (thematic_auto.py:1498-1521) — natural place to add a 'super-cluster' fold (ai_leaders+ai_infrastructure+memory_hbm+datacenter_power+optical_network -> one AI_COMPLEX) for a cluster-level count/weight cap
- _correlation_guard_for_book (thematic_auto.py:5264) — already implemented; flipping THEMATIC_CORRELATION_GUARD default to on and lowering the 0.85 threshold is a ready-made cross-name diversification lever
- portfolio_policy.evaluate() hierarchy (portfolio_policy.py:212) — a sector/cluster-balance tier can be inserted (e.g. down-rank or suppress a candidate whose sector/cluster is already over a target weight) since it already loops candidates best-first
- _portfolio_aware_dollar (thematic_auto.py:4322) — already assembles the full book with real per-ticker sectors + candidate sector + weights; the data needed for any sector-spread decision is already gathered here
- _check_thematic_exits (thematic_auto.py:2985) — the only exit engine; a portfolio-shape-aware rebalancing exit (trim weakest name in the most over-weight sector/cluster) would attach here, where it currently has none

### Sector/theme classification for the thematic (social-momentum) system — how a ticker's market slice is known at pick-time and size-time

**Flow:** There are TWO parallel, loosely-coupled classifiers, and the strong one (theme) is NOT the one wired to a real diversification cap.

1) THEME (the primary "which slice of market" tag, present everywhere). Source is the free LLM pick. `_ai_pick`'s prompt hard-constrains theme to one of exactly 12 strings (web/api/thematic_auto.py:1674: ai_leaders, ai_infrastructure, optical_network, memory_hbm, datacenter_power, nuclear_energy, space_defense, quantum_future, critical_minerals, reshoring, fintech_consumer, future_tech). The LLM's raw string is folded to a canonical key by `_canonical_theme` (1515) via `_THEME_ALIASES` (1498); anything unrecognized collapses to the `future_tech` catch-all. `_sanitize_picks` (1600) and `_validate_pick` (1450) apply this. A static reverse-lookup map `THEMES_MAP` (1417, ~12 themes x ~6-7 hardcoded mega/large-cap tickers ≈ 75 names) exists but is used ONLY as a fallback via `_guess_theme` (1432) when the LLM theme is invalid. Theme is stamped on the signal at scan/pick-time (3871) and copied onto the persisted paper position at approve/size-time (5859). So theme IS available at BOTH pick-time and size-time.

2) GICS SECTOR (the real market-sector taxonomy, used only by the money sizer). Source is `_sector_of` (4242): yfinance `info['sector']` first, then free-LLM `_ai_sector_fill` (4225) if yfinance is empty (common for small-caps), cached persistently to sector_cache.json. 11 GICS sectors (`_GICS_SECTORS`, 4209). CRITICAL: `_sector_of` has only two callers (grep-confirmed) — its own AI-fill and `_portfolio_aware_dollar` (4322). It is computed ONLY at approve/size-time, inside a 12-second timeout (4363), for the whole book at once, and is NEVER persisted — the position dict literally stores `"sector": "thematic"` (5859), a constant string, not the GICS sector. On timeout or yfinance/AI failure the sectors dict is empty and every sector becomes None.

Where each is actually enforced: the ONLY always-on diversification control is a per-THEME cap `PORTFOLIO_MAX_PER_THEME = 3` (2444), checked at approve (5835) by counting open positions with matching `theme`. The GICS sector feeds a soft/hard sizer cap `max_sector_pct=30%` in `size_position` (position_sizer.py:234-242) but only at size-time, only when sector is known, and it fails OPEN (242: unknown sector → sector_room = math.inf → cap removed). The scan-time `size_factor` (portfolio_policy.py:182) is `conviction x concentration-room` where room is a function of TOTAL position count only — completely blind to sector/theme.

**Sector awareness:** Two disjoint notions of "sector" that never reconcile. (a) `theme` = a 12-bucket in-house taxonomy from a free LLM, present on every signal and position, enforced by a hard per-theme cap of 3. (b) `sector` = real GICS from yfinance+AI, computed only at approve-time for sizing, never stored (positions carry the literal string "thematic" as their sector). The one hard, always-on control is per-theme; the one real GICS control is size-time-only and fail-open. The taxonomy itself is the deepest problem: ~8 of the 12 themes are AI/semiconductor-adjacent (ai_leaders, ai_infrastructure, optical_network, memory_hbm, datacenter_power, quantum_future, plus nuclear_energy and critical_minerals/reshoring which exist as AI-datacenter/chip-supply plays). There is no healthcare/biotech proper (future_tech holds a few gene-editing names), no consumer staples, no financials proper, no energy proper, no real estate, no industrials proper — so the classifier has almost nowhere to route a non-tech idea even if the crowd surfaced one.

**Concentration risks:**
- Per-theme cap of 3 (thematic_auto.py:2444/5835) is the ONLY always-on control, but ~8 of 12 themes are AI/semis-adjacent — you can hold 3 ai_leaders + 3 ai_infrastructure + 3 memory_hbm + 3 datacenter_power = 12 positions that are all effectively the AI/semiconductor trade and never trip any cap.
- The 12-theme taxonomy (thematic_auto.py:1674) has no real non-tech buckets (no proper healthcare, financials, energy, staples, real estate, industrials); any idea that doesn't fit falls into the 'future_tech' catch-all, so the classifier structurally funnels the book toward AI/tech.
- GICS sector cap (position_sizer.py:234-242) fails OPEN: unknown sector -> sector_room = math.inf, so on the 12s enrichment timeout (thematic_auto.py:4363) or any yfinance/AI-fill miss, the 30% sector cap silently disappears for the whole book.
- GICS sector is never persisted — positions store the constant 'sector':'thematic' (thematic_auto.py:5859) — so the sizer must recompute the entire book's real sectors from yfinance on every single approval; slow/flaky and easily degraded to no-cap.
- GICS sector is unavailable at pick/scan-time entirely (_sector_of has no scan-path caller), so scoring, ranking, and the size_factor stamp are blind to real sector concentration.
- Scan-time size_factor (portfolio_policy.py:182) shrinks new size only by TOTAL position count, not by sector/theme — a book that is 100% AI is throttled identically to a perfectly diversified one.
- Active concentration AMPLIFIER: thematic_portfolio.py:204-207 scores premium_themes {ai_leaders, ai_infrastructure, memory_hbm, datacenter_power} at 9.0 vs 5.5 for everything else — the quality scoring literally rewards piling into AI/semis.
- The correlation guard (_correlation_guard_for_book, thematic_auto.py:5271) is DEFAULT-OFF and fail-open; the sizer's correlation_factor is a soft shrink (not a cap) and needs price history that is best-effort — so highly-correlated AI names are only weakly discouraged.
- theme comes from a free Cloudflare/OpenRouter model with no schema guarantee beyond post-hoc clamping; a mislabeled or catch-all 'future_tech' theme defeats the per-theme cap, and the static THEMES_MAP floor covers only ~75 mega-cap tickers.

**Diversification hooks:**
- Persist the real GICS sector on the position at approve-time: replace the constant 'sector':'thematic' at thematic_auto.py:5859 with _sector_of(ticker) — this single change makes book-wide GICS available without per-approval recompute and lets a real per-sector cap read it.
- The approve-time cap block (thematic_auto.py:5827-5838) already counts theme_count and raises cap_reason — add a parallel GICS-sector count/cap here alongside PORTFOLIO_MAX_PER_THEME (2444); it is the natural home for a hard, always-on per-sector limit.
- _portfolio_aware_dollar (thematic_auto.py:4322) already builds BookPosition sectors and calls the sizer — make its 12s enrichment fail-CLOSED (treat unknown sector as its own bucket or block sizing) instead of degrading to neutral.
- position_sizer.size_position sector cap (position_sizer.py:234-242, max_sector_pct default 30, SIZER_MAX_SECTOR_PCT env at 103) is a ready-made per-sector clamp — flip line 242 from 'unknown -> math.inf' to fail-closed, and it becomes a real control.
- Broaden the theme taxonomy: the AI prompt's 12-theme allowlist (thematic_auto.py:1674) + THEMES_MAP (1417) + _THEME_ALIASES (1498) are the single source of buckets — adding genuine non-tech themes (healthcare, financials, energy, staples, industrials) is the root-cause fix so ideas can land outside AI.
- Generalize PORTFOLIO_MAX_PER_THEME into a per-GICS-sector cap (thematic_auto.py:2444) once sector is persisted, so the always-on hard control keys off real market sectors, not the AI-skewed theme taxonomy.
- Feed sector/theme concentration into scan-time size_factor (portfolio_policy.py:182) so new-idea sizing shrinks when the book is already heavy in that slice, not just when total count is high.
- Remove/invert the premium-theme scoring boost (thematic_portfolio.py:204-207) so scoring stops rewarding AI concentration; could become a diversification BONUS for under-represented sectors.
- Turn on and harden the existing correlation guard (thematic_auto.py:5271, THEMATIC_MAX_CORRELATION) and the sizer correlation_factor (position_sizer.py:161) as a statistical backstop for when sector/theme labels disagree.


## Appendix B — Diversification research (agent findings)

### Two-granularity "diversification budget" that bounds the tail of a naturally-clustering momentum book without killing conviction. Every name is tagged with (a) a MACRO CLUSTER — the ~6-bucket collapse of the 12 fake themes via a new `_THEME_MACRO` map, derived from the ALWAYS-present `theme` label — and (b) a real GICS SECTOR (`_sector_of`). Each bucket gets BOTH a hard NAMES count cap AND a hard DOLLAR budget (% of account), plus a SOFT size-decay ramp: the first few names in a cluster size at full conviction, each marginal name past the soft cap is shrunk geometrically, and beyond the hard count/dollar ceiling new same-cluster names are deferred (propose-only, human-forceable). Because the PRIMARY cap keys off `theme` (free, always present) and not the slow/flaky yfinance sector call, it NEVER fails open — fixing the `sector_room = math.inf` hole at position_sizer.py:242. GICS is the orthogonal cross-check. The rule is applied at three stages (rank → pick → approve) and on the live Fidelity leg, so diversification survives even if one stage is bypassed.

**Mechanism:** NEW pure module `tradingagents/portfolio/diversification.py` (mirrors the pure/sync/network-free contract of position_sizer.py & portfolio_policy.py) + a `_THEME_MACRO` map next to THEMES_MAP (thematic_auto.py:1417).

MACRO MAP (default, env-overridable via DIVERSIFY_THEME_MACRO_JSON):
  ai_complex = {ai_leaders, ai_infrastructure, optical_network, memory_hbm, datacenter_power, quantum_future, nuclear_energy}
  materials_supply = {critical_minerals}; industrials = {reshoring}; defense_aero = {space_defense};
  fintech_consumer = {fintech_consumer}; other_growth = {future_tech}.  `_macro_of(theme)->cluster`.

CORE PURE FUNCTION:
  @dataclass DiversifyConfig.from_env(): max_cluster_pct=35, max_names_per_cluster=4, soft_names_per_cluster=2,
    cluster_decay=0.6, max_sector_pct=30, max_names_per_sector=4.
  def _bucket_key(sector, ticker): return sector.strip().lower() if sector else f"unknown:{ticker.lower()}"   # FAIL-CLOSED: unknown GICS becomes its own singleton bucket (never math.inf, never a false block)
  def diversification_room(cand_cluster, cand_sector, cand_ticker, book, account_value, cfg) -> (dollar_cap: float, decay_mult: float, reason: str):
      cl_n  = sum(1 for b in book if b.cluster == cand_cluster)
      cl_d  = sum(b.dollars for b in book if b.cluster == cand_cluster)
      sk    = _bucket_key(cand_sector, cand_ticker)
      sec_n = sum(1 for b in book if _bucket_key(b.sector, b.ticker) == sk)
      sec_d = sum(b.dollars for b in book if _bucket_key(b.sector, b.ticker) == sk)
      if cl_n  >= cfg.max_names_per_cluster:  return (0.0, 0.0, f"cluster {cand_cluster} at {cl_n} names")   # HARD count cap
      if sec_n >= cfg.max_names_per_sector:   return (0.0, 0.0, f"sector {sk} at {sec_n} names")
      cl_room  = account_value * cfg.max_cluster_pct/100.0 - cl_d
      sec_room = account_value * cfg.max_sector_pct/100.0 - sec_d
      cap = max(0.0, min(cl_room, sec_room))                                                                 # HARD dollar budget
      if cap <= 0: return (0.0, 0.0, "cluster/sector $ budget full")
      decay = cfg.cluster_decay ** max(0, cl_n - cfg.soft_names_per_cluster)                                 # SOFT tail ramp: 1.0, 1.0, 0.6, 0.36...
      return (cap, decay, "")

WIRING (all hooks already exist in the map):
 1. position_sizer.size_position (position_sizer.py:249-257): add `cluster` to SizingCandidate/BookPosition, multiply `raw` by `decay`, and append ("cluster_cap", cl_room) to the min()-limits list; replace the unknown->math.inf sector branch (line 242) with the `_bucket_key` fail-closed version. Dollar-truthful home.
 2. Pick loop (thematic_auto.py:3791): seed a `{cluster: n}` / `{sector: n}` tally from `_existing_portfolio` + `_already_pending`, increment per created signal; before the append at :3865 compute `cl = _macro_of(pick['theme'])` and (cached) `_sector_of(t)`, and `continue` when the hard count cap is hit — this is the "don't even propose the 4th AI name" rule at the single chokepoint. Cluster comes from `theme` so it works even if `_sector_of` is cold.
 3. _merge_signals final sort (thematic_auto.py:1376): round-robin/interleave `ranked` by `_macro_of(_guess_theme(t))` before `[:25]`, so the top-20 handed to the LLM is already sector-spread.
 4. _build_ai_pick_prompt (thematic_auto.py:1633): add "diversify — at most N names per macro-theme, spread across sectors" (soft, free, pairs with the hard downstream caps).
 5. approve ladder (thematic_auto.py:5833-5838): add a cluster COUNT + cluster/sector DOLLAR cap alongside PORTFOLIO_MAX_PER_THEME as a backstop, setting cap_reason.
 6. Persist (thematic_auto.py:5859): replace `"sector":"thematic"` with `_sector_of(ticker)` and add `"macro_cluster": _macro_of(theme)` so the book's real buckets are readable without per-approval recompute.
 7. Live Fidelity leg (thematic_auto.py:5892): honor cap_reason (skip the real order when a diversification cap blocked the paper leg) OR run diversification_room against the unified real+paper book before `_size_fidelity_position` — closes the real-money gap.
 8. thematic_portfolio.py:205: drop the premium-AI theme boost (9.0) so scoring stops rewarding concentration; optionally invert to a small bonus for under-represented clusters.

Everything except the two already-cached lookups (`_sector_of`, paper-state read) is pure list/dict arithmetic and unit-testable in isolation.

**Rules:**
- MACRO-CLUSTER NAMES CAP (hard, primary): at most DIVERSIFY_MAX_NAMES_PER_CLUSTER=4 open+pending names share one macro cluster. Cluster is derived from the always-present `theme` via `_THEME_MACRO`, so this cap can never fail open. This is what converts the currently-useless PORTFOLIO_MAX_PER_THEME=3 into a real control by collapsing the 7 fake AI sub-themes into one `ai_complex` bucket.
- MACRO-CLUSTER DOLLAR BUDGET (hard): no macro cluster may exceed DIVERSIFY_MAX_CLUSTER_PCT=35% of account value. Sizing is clamped to the remaining cluster room (a min()-limit in the sizer), not just blocked.
- GICS-SECTOR NAMES CAP (hard, cross-check): at most DIVERSIFY_MAX_NAMES_PER_SECTOR=4 names in one real GICS sector — catches the case where two different-looking themes are actually the same sector.
- GICS-SECTOR DOLLAR BUDGET (hard): reuse SIZER_MAX_SECTOR_PCT=30% but make it FAIL-CLOSED — unknown sector becomes its own singleton bucket `unknown:<ticker>` instead of math.inf, so a timed-out enrichment can no longer silently delete the cap.
- SOFT TAIL RAMP (allow conviction, cap the tail): the first DIVERSIFY_SOFT_NAMES_PER_CLUSTER=2 names in a cluster size at full conviction; each name past that is multiplied by DIVERSIFY_CLUSTER_DECAY^(k)=0.6, 0.36, ... so the hot narrative can still be the biggest bucket but every marginal name adds less. Names shrunk below SIZER_MIN_DOLLAR are naturally skipped by the existing sizer.
- PICK-TIME ENFORCEMENT (don't even propose the tail): the `for pick in picks:` loop keeps a running cluster/sector tally seeded from the unified book and `continue`s on the hard count cap before creating the pending signal — the human sees an already-diversified slate.
- RANK-TIME INTERLEAVE: `_merge_signals` round-robins the ranked list by macro cluster before truncating to 25, so a monolithic hot narrative can't monopolize the top-20 the LLM picks from.
- APPROVE-TIME BACKSTOP: the same cluster count + dollar caps run in the approve cap ladder for any signal that bypassed pick-time (manual add, force, policy fallback).
- LIVE-LEG PARITY: the Fidelity order path honors cap_reason / re-runs the cluster check against the unified real+paper book, so a paper-blocked over-concentration can't still place real money.
- PROPOSE-ONLY OVERRIDE: every diversification block is advisory — `force=true` on approve bypasses it exactly like the existing 'No portfolio room' path, so the human keeps final authority.
- STRUCTURAL GUARANTEE: with a per-cluster names cap C and MAX_POSITIONS=N the full book always spans at least ceil(N/C) clusters (10/4 -> >=3 clusters; set C=3 for >=4). Diversification is guaranteed by construction, not by hope.
- PERSIST THE BUCKETS: store real `sector` + `macro_cluster` on the position at approve-time so caps read them directly instead of recomputing the whole book's sectors from yfinance on every approval.

**Fit:** Strong fit. (1) Propose-only/HIL: every cap is advisory — pick-time simply doesn't create the tail signal, sizing shrinks rather than hard-walls, and `force=true` already exists to override, so the human still gets final say; the machine just hands them a pre-diversified slate instead of six semis names. (2) Social-momentum clusters by nature: the soft decay ramp + tail ceiling is purpose-built for this — it does NOT fight the hot narrative (the 4 best AI ideas can still be your largest bucket, up to 35% and full conviction on the first two) but it bounds the tail so the book can't become 100% one factor. (3) It fixes the specific rot in THIS system: the cluster key is derived from the `theme` string every signal already carries, turning the dead PORTFOLIO_MAX_PER_THEME cap into a live one, and it never fails open because it doesn't depend on the flaky yfinance sector call the way the current 30% GICS cap does. (4) It matches the repo's own pattern — a pure, sync, network-free rule engine (like holdings_brain/portfolio_policy/position_sizer) as the safety floor, with the LLM prompt as a soft nudge on top. (5) It plugs into the exact hooks the code map already identified (pick loop, sizer min()-limits, approve ladder, live leg), so it's a bounded change, not a rewrite.

**Knobs:** DIVERSIFY_ENABLED (default true) — master switch for the whole diversification budget layer, DIVERSIFY_MAX_NAMES_PER_CLUSTER (default 4) — hard count cap of names sharing one macro cluster (the primary AI-concentration control), DIVERSIFY_MAX_CLUSTER_PCT (default 35) — hard % of account any one macro cluster may hold, DIVERSIFY_SOFT_NAMES_PER_CLUSTER (default 2) — names in a cluster before the size-decay ramp kicks in, DIVERSIFY_CLUSTER_DECAY (default 0.6) — geometric size multiplier per name past the soft cap (1.0, 1.0, 0.6, 0.36...), DIVERSIFY_MAX_NAMES_PER_SECTOR (default 4) — hard count cap of names in one real GICS sector (orthogonal cross-check), SIZER_MAX_SECTOR_PCT (existing, default 30) — reused as the GICS dollar budget; behavior changed to fail-CLOSED via per-ticker unknown bucket, DIVERSIFY_THEME_MACRO_JSON (default '' -> built-in map) — JSON override of the theme->macro-cluster mapping so the taxonomy can evolve without a code change, DIVERSIFY_PICKTIME (default true) — enforce hard count caps at the pick loop (propose an already-diversified slate) vs approve-time-only, DIVERSIFY_ENFORCE_LIVE (default true) — apply the cluster/sector caps to the live Fidelity leg (honor cap_reason / re-check unified book) to close the real-money gap

### Correlation- and theme-cluster diversification: a three-layer concentration guard that treats the "one big AI bet" problem as a CLUSTERING problem, not a per-ticker problem. Layer 1 (primary, data-free, always-on): fold the 12 narrative themes into ~5 MACRO-clusters via a new `_THEME_MACRO` map and cap both name-count and dollar-weight per macro-cluster — this is what actually stops 3xNVDA-adjacent themes from stacking into a monolithic AI book. Layer 2 (statistical backstop, needs return history): cluster the unified book+candidate by realized-return correlation (single-linkage union-find) and cap dollar exposure per EMPIRICAL cluster, catching concentration the labels miss. Layer 3 (sizing penalty): replace the sizer's current single-worst-pairwise correlation shrink with a book-weighted SUMMED-correlation load plus an effective-number-of-bets (N_eff) advisory on the HIL card. The macro-theme layer is the floor the correlation layer degrades TO when price data is missing, so the guard never silently vanishes.

**Mechanism:** Reuses existing pure primitives: correlation.py `pct_returns` (:63), `pearson` (:82), `max_correlation` (:99); position_sizer.py `correlation_factor` (:161) and the `min()` hard-limit list in `size_position` (:249-257); the `_closes_map` batched downloader (thematic_auto.py:4269) already called inside `_portfolio_aware_dollar` (:4322).

NEW PRIMITIVE A — theme->macro fold (data-free). Add next to `_THEME_ALIASES` (thematic_auto.py:1498):
`_THEME_MACRO = {ai_leaders, ai_infrastructure, optical_network, memory_hbm, datacenter_power, nuclear_energy, quantum_future -> "ai_complex"; critical_minerals -> "resources"; reshoring -> "industrials"; space_defense -> "defense"; fintech_consumer -> "fintech"; future_tech -> "biotech_frontier"}`.
`def macro_of(theme): return _THEME_MACRO.get(_canonical_theme(theme), "other")`. Membership (esp. nuclear/quantum/minerals) is env-overridable because that judgment IS the whole lever.

NEW PRIMITIVE B — correlation clustering in correlation.py (pure, injected returns):
```
def correlation_clusters(returns_by_ticker, link=0.65, min_overlap=20):
    tks=list(returns_by_ticker); parent={t:t for t in tks}
    def find(x):
        while parent[x]!=x: parent[x]=parent[parent[x]]; x=parent[x]
        return x
    for i in range(len(tks)):
        for j in range(i+1,len(tks)):
            a,b=returns_by_ticker[tks[i]],returns_by_ticker[tks[j]]
            if min(len(a),len(b))<min_overlap: continue      # unknown -> DON'T merge
            r=pearson(a,b)
            if r is not None and abs(r)>=link:
                parent[find(tks[i])]=find(tks[j])            # single-linkage union
    return {t:find(t) for t in tks}                          # ticker -> cluster id
```
Small book (<=~21 names) -> <=210 pairwise pearsons over ~60 pts: trivial, deterministic, offline-testable.

NEW PRIMITIVE C — weighted summed-correlation load + effective-N (replaces max-pairwise):
```
def corr_load(cand_rets, book):            # book: {tk:(weight_frac, rets)}
    num=den=0.0
    for tk,(w,rets) in book.items():
        r=pearson(cand_rets,rets)
        if r is None: continue
        num += w*max(0.0,r); den += w
    return (num/den) if den>0 else None     # weighted avg POSITIVE corr, None=unknown
def effective_bets(weights, C):             # C[i][j] corr (unknown off-diag -> 0.0), diag 1
    s=sum(weights); q=sum(weights[i]*weights[j]*C[i][j] for i in R for j in R)
    return (s*s/q) if q>0 else len(weights) # HHI-of-correlation; ~1 = one bet
```
Upgrade `correlation_factor` to take `load` instead of `max_corr`: 1.0 below `corr_threshold` (0.70, position_sizer.py:78), scaling to `1-corr_penalty_max` (0.50, :79) as load->1 — a name at 0.6 corr to FIVE holdings (max=0.6, today unpenalized) now shrinks correctly.

WIRING — single injection point is `_portfolio_aware_dollar` (thematic_auto.py:4322-4392), which already fetches book+candidate closes and computes `max_correlation` (:4370). Extend its enrich block to also: (a) build `returns_by_ticker` from `_closes_map` output via `pct_returns`; (b) `clusters=correlation_clusters({**book_rets, cand:cand_rets})`; (c) `cluster_weight = sum(BookPosition.weight_pct for tk in book if clusters[tk]==clusters[cand])`; (d) `load=corr_load(...)`. Pass three new fields into `SizingCandidate`: `cluster_weight_pct`, `corr_load`, `macro_cluster`. In `size_position`, add ONE limit to the min() list (:249-257): `("cluster_cap", av*max_cluster_pct/100 - cluster_dollars)`. The smallest-binding-limit machinery already reports it as `binding_constraint` in the human note.

ALWAYS-ON HARD FLOOR — at the approve cap ladder (thematic_auto.py:5827-5838), alongside `theme_count`/`PORTFOLIO_MAX_PER_THEME` (:5830,:5835) add:
`macro=macro_of(sig["theme"]); macro_count=sum(1 for p in open_positions.values() if macro_of(p.get("theme"))==macro and p.get("_source","").startswith("thematic"))`; `if macro_count>=MAX_PER_MACRO_CLUSTER: cap_reason=f"{macro} cluster at max {N} names"`. This needs ZERO market data.

GRACEFUL DEGRADATION LADDER (the crux): cluster_room = (empirical-cluster room if returns present) ELSE (macro-cluster dollar room computed from theme tags alone). Critically, flip the sibling of position_sizer.py:242 so a missing cluster does NOT default to `math.inf`; it defaults to the macro-theme room, which is always computable. So: full returns -> empirical clusters + summed load + N_eff; partial returns -> cluster on what loads, unknown names fall back to their macro bucket (union the two); ZERO returns (the 12s timeout, exact case that today disables the GICS cap) -> macro count + dollar cap only, fail-CLOSED to theme. Never no-cap.

**Rules:**
- Fold the 12 narrative themes into ~5 macro-clusters via a new `_THEME_MACRO` map (next to `_THEME_ALIASES`, thematic_auto.py:1498); ai_leaders + ai_infrastructure + optical_network + memory_hbm + datacenter_power (+ optionally nuclear_energy, quantum_future) all collapse to ONE `ai_complex` bucket so 3+3+3+3 same-macro names can't stack.
- Always-on, data-free HARD count cap: max N names per macro-cluster (default 4), enforced in the approve cap ladder (thematic_auto.py:5835) right beside the existing PORTFOLIO_MAX_PER_THEME=3 check, using only the `theme` tag every signal already carries.
- Always-on macro-cluster DOLLAR cap: max X% of account per macro-cluster (default 35%), computed from theme tags only — needs no yfinance, so it can never silently disable like the GICS cap does.
- When >= min_overlap (default 20) days of returns exist for candidate + book: build single-linkage correlation clusters (|corr| >= link_threshold, default 0.65) over the UNIFIED book+candidate via `correlation_clusters`, and cap per-empirical-cluster dollar exposure as one more limit in size_position's min() list (position_sizer.py:249-257).
- Replace the sizer's single-worst-pairwise `correlation_factor` (position_sizer.py:161, fed by max_corr) with a book-weight-weighted SUMMED positive-correlation load; a name correlated 0.6 to five holdings must be shrunk even though its max pairwise is below threshold.
- Compute portfolio effective-number-of-bets N_eff = (sum w)^2 / (w^T C w) and surface it on the HIL propose card; warn/advise-block below min_effective_bets (default 4) but do NOT auto-hard-block on it (correlation is noisy) — the hard blocks live in the theme-macro layer.
- Degrade gracefully theme-first: returns present -> empirical clusters; returns missing -> the macro-narrative bucket IS the cluster and its dollar cap still binds. Flip the fail-open default (position_sizer.py:242 pattern) so cluster_room falls back to macro-room, never math.inf.
- Enforce the macro count + dollar cap on the LIVE Fidelity leg too (thematic_auto.py:5892 / _size_fidelity_position, fidelity.py:1925), because the paper cap ladder demonstrably does NOT gate the real order — read cap_reason there or re-check the macro cap before placing.
- Persist the resolved macro_cluster (and real GICS sector) on the stored position instead of the constant 'thematic' (thematic_auto.py:5859) so the caps read it back cheaply without a full per-approval recompute.
- Flip `_correlation_guard_for_book` (thematic_auto.py:5264) from default-off/max-pairwise to a summed-corr OR empirical-cluster check as a redundant approve-time backstop, keeping fail-open ONLY there since the theme-macro layer is the real floor.

**Fit:** Strong fit, with the emphasis deliberately inverted from what you'd do for a systematic fund. (1) Propose-only/HIL: every layer emits a human-readable reason — macro cap gives cap_reason 'ai_complex cluster at max 4 names', the sizer's binding_constraint already prints 'bound by cluster_cap', and N_eff is a single legible 'this book is really ~2 bets' number on the card. That matches the existing cap_reason (thematic_auto.py:5832) and SizingResult.notes plumbing exactly — no new UX contract. (2) Social-momentum: buzz clusters BY NARRATIVE, so the theme-macro cap is the natural primitive — the momentum literally IS the cluster, and the tag is free and always present. Correlation is the statistical confirmation for when the LLM mislabels a name or dumps it in the future_tech catch-all. (3) Small book (~10, hard 20): clustering is a <=21x21 matrix (cheap), N_eff is meaningful, and 'max 4 names / 35% per macro' produces real behavioral change rather than rounding error. (4) Because correlation on 60d of hot momentum names is noisy and spikes toward 1.0 in every selloff (procyclical — it would over-block exactly in a drawdown), the design keeps the HARD blocks on the stable theme layer and uses correlation mainly as a SOFT shrink + advisory, which is the right risk posture for a book a human is approving name-by-name. The one real misfit it must fix, not paper over: the live Fidelity leg bypasses these caps today, so 'propose-only diversification' is a lie for real money until the macro cap is also enforced at thematic_auto.py:5892.

**Knobs:** THEMATIC_MAX_PER_MACRO_CLUSTER — hard name-count cap per macro-cluster (default 4); the data-free always-on floor at approve., SIZER_MAX_CLUSTER_PCT — max % of account per correlation/macro cluster (default 35); new limit in size_position min() list, env-tunable via SizerConfig.from_env., SIZER_CLUSTER_LINK_THRESHOLD — |corr| to merge two names into one empirical cluster (default 0.65)., SIZER_CORR_THRESHOLD / SIZER_CORR_PENALTY_MAX — reuse existing (0.70 / 0.50, position_sizer.py:78-79) but now feed the SUMMED corr load, not max pairwise., SIZER_MIN_EFFECTIVE_BETS — advisory N_eff floor surfaced on the HIL card (default 4); warn, not auto-block., THEMATIC_CORR_LOOKBACK_DAYS — return window for pairwise corr (default 60, matches max_correlation lookback)., THEMATIC_CORR_MIN_OVERLAP — min overlapping return points to trust a pairwise corr / allow a cluster merge (default 20)., THEMATIC_CLUSTER_FAIL_MODE — degradation policy when returns missing: theme_macro (default, degrade cluster_room to macro-theme room) | closed (block) | open (legacy math.inf, discouraged)., THEMATIC_MACRO_MAP_OVERRIDE — optional JSON to reassign borderline themes (nuclear_energy/quantum_future/critical_minerals) into or out of ai_complex without a code change., THEMATIC_CORRELATION_GUARD / THEMATIC_MAX_CORRELATION — existing approve-time backstop (thematic_auto.py:5261,:5278); flip default on and retune threshold now that it's redundant to the sizer cluster cap.

### MACRO-CLUSTER BUDGET + DRIFT TILT — a "target-weights-with-drift-rebalancing" method, adapted for a propose-only book, keyed off a static theme→macro-cluster fold (NOT GICS, NOT risk-parity/ERC).

Of the three researched families: (1) equal-risk-contribution / risk-parity across sectors is REJECTED — it needs a covariance matrix (per-name vol + cross-correlations) estimated from 6mo closes, which in this system loads best-effort inside the same fragile 12s asyncio.wait_for that already fails open (thematic_auto.py:4363/4373); on a 10-20 name book that covariance is noisy/ill-conditioned (needs Ledoit-Wolf shrinkage), the solver is iterative and OPAQUE on a HIL card ("why is my size $312?"), and — fatally — ERC on GICS sectors still calls a 100%-AI-supply-chain book "balanced" because the AI trade spans Technology/Utilities/Materials/Comm-Services. (3) capacity-aware (ADV) allocation is ORTHOGONAL, not a substitute — it bounds single-name liquidity and is ALREADY implemented as the `liquidity_adv` limit (position_sizer.py:254); keep it, it doesn't spread the book across sections. (2) target-weights-with-drift is the winner, but a propose-only book cannot autonomously sell to rebalance, so "rebalancing" is re-expressed as ENTRY-TIME enforcement: a hard per-cluster dollar BUDGET cap + a soft drift TILT that shrinks new money as a cluster fills + a pick-time name COUNT backstop. The decisive robustness win over every GICS-based control: the cluster label is derived from the `theme` string already on every signal/position via a static dict — it is NETWORK-FREE, so unlike the GICS sector_room (which silently becomes math.inf whenever yfinance/the 12s enrich dies, position_sizer.py:242) the cluster cap is trustworthy exactly when the data pipeline is degraded.

**Mechanism:** Three composable additions; NONE replaces the conviction×quality sizer — two are one-liners into the existing size_position composition, one is a pick-loop counter.

STEP 0 — NEW primitive next to THEMES_MAP (thematic_auto.py:1417). The cheap lever that collapses the fake-diverse 12-theme taxonomy into real macro buckets:
```python
_THEME_MACRO = {
  "ai_leaders":"ai_complex","ai_infrastructure":"ai_complex","optical_network":"ai_complex",
  "memory_hbm":"ai_complex","datacenter_power":"ai_complex","nuclear_energy":"ai_complex",
  "quantum_future":"ai_complex","critical_minerals":"materials_supply","reshoring":"industrials",
  "space_defense":"defense","fintech_consumer":"fintech","future_tech":"frontier_bio",
}
_GICS_TO_MACRO = {"Technology":"ai_complex","Communication Services":"ai_complex",
  "Utilities":"ai_complex","Materials":"materials_supply","Industrials":"industrials",
  "Financials":"fintech","Health Care":"frontier_bio",  # coarse fallback for real holdings w/o a theme
  "Energy":"energy","Consumer Discretionary":"consumer","Consumer Staples":"consumer","Real Estate":"reit"}
def _macro_cluster(theme, sector=None):
    c = _THEME_MACRO.get(_canonical_theme(theme))           # network-free primary
    return c or _GICS_TO_MACRO.get((sector or "").strip(), "other")
```

STEP A — SOFT DRIFT TILT: a new factor centred on 1.0, structurally identical to correlation_factor (position_sizer.py:161). Give SizingCandidate/BookPosition a `cluster` field and SizerConfig `max_cluster_pct=35.0, div_floor=0.30`. In size_position, before line 211:
```python
def cluster_div_factor(cluster, existing, av, cfg):
    if not cluster or av<=0: return 1.0
    cur = sum(av*_finite(p.weight_pct)/100.0 for p in existing
              if (p.cluster or "").lower()==cluster.lower())
    util = (cur/av)/(cfg.max_cluster_pct/100.0)     # 0 empty .. 1 at budget
    return max(cfg.div_floor, min(1.0, 1.0-util))   # full cluster -> 0.30x
f_div = cluster_div_factor(candidate.cluster, existing, av, cfg)
raw   = base * f_conv * f_q * f_vol * f_corr * f_div   # EXTEND line 211 — nothing removed
```
Empty cluster ->1.0x (idea untouched); half-full ->~0.5x; full ->floored 0.30x. This tilts NEW money toward under-owned clusters WITHOUT ever blocking a high-conviction name.

STEP B — HARD BUDGET CAP: one more entry in the existing MIN-of-limits list (position_sizer.py:249-257). Before `binding, size = min(limits...)`:
```python
cluster_room = math.inf
if candidate.cluster:
    cdol = sum(av*_finite(p.weight_pct)/100.0 for p in existing
               if (p.cluster or "").lower()==candidate.cluster.lower())
    cluster_room = max(0.0, av*cfg.max_cluster_pct/100.0 - cdol)
limits.append(("cluster_cap", cluster_room))        # sits beside sector_cap/heat/cash
```
"Smallest binding limit wins" machinery already exists — a name that would push ai_complex past 35% is bound to the remaining room (or 0 -> skipped via the existing <min_dollar branch). Because `cluster` comes from _macro_cluster(theme) it is ALWAYS known (worst case its own future_tech/other bucket) -> this cap does NOT fail open, unlike sector_room.

WIRING (thematic_auto.py:4375-4388, _portfolio_aware_dollar): set cand `cluster=_macro_cluster(sig.get("theme"))` and each BookPosition `cluster=_macro_cluster(p.get("theme"))`. The paper position dict already carries `theme` (stamped at :5859 alongside the useless sector:"thematic"), so this is a pure dict read — it works even when the 12s sector/close enrichment times out.

STEP C — PICK-TIME COUNT BACKSTOP: in the `for pick in picks:` loop (thematic_auto.py:3791), seed `cluster_counts` from open `_existing_portfolio` + carried pending; near the MIN_COMPOSITE_SCORE gate (:3860) add `clu=_macro_cluster(pick["theme"]); if cluster_counts[clu]>=MAX_NAMES_PER_CLUSTER: continue`, and `cluster_counts[clu]+=1` after append. This is the ONLY guard that also bites the explicit-dollar / size_factor / _conviction_dollar branches that skip the sizer, and it works when account_value==0 (sizer no-ops). Same counter, evaluated again at approve-time (:5830 ladder) must gate BOTH the paper leg AND the live Fidelity leg (:5892) to close the documented live-leg gap where cap_reason is ignored.

**Rules:**
- CLUSTER, NOT GICS, is the diversification unit: fold the 12 narrative themes into ~6 macro-clusters via a static _THEME_MACRO dict (ai_leaders+ai_infrastructure+optical_network+memory_hbm+datacenter_power+nuclear_energy+quantum_future -> one 'ai_complex'). This converts the useless per-theme cap into a real concentration cap.
- HARD dollar budget: no single macro-cluster may exceed MAX_CLUSTER_PCT (default 35%) of account value; enforce as one extra ('cluster_cap', cluster_room) entry in position_sizer.size_position's min() limits list (position_sizer.py:249-257).
- SOFT drift tilt: multiply raw by cluster_div_factor = clamp(1 - cur_cluster_weight/(MAX_CLUSTER_PCT), DIV_FLOOR=0.30, 1.0) — a new factor in the raw product at position_sizer.py:211, centred on 1.0, identical in shape to the existing correlation_factor. Shrinks (never blocks) as a cluster fills.
- COUNT backstop at pick time: in the for-pick loop (thematic_auto.py:3791) maintain cluster_counts seeded from the open book; `continue` before creating the (MAX_NAMES_PER_CLUSTER=4)th pending signal in one cluster. This is the only guard covering the non-sizer sizing branches and the account_value==0 case.
- Cluster label MUST stay network-free: derive it from the position's already-stored `theme` field via _macro_cluster(), NOT from _sector_of()/yfinance. This is why the cap survives the 12s enrichment timeout that disables the GICS sector cap.
- COMPOSE, do not replace: conviction_scale (position_sizer.py:205), quality_factor (:206), inverse_vol (:207), the total-count size_factor (portfolio_policy.py:182) and per-position 10% cap all remain untouched; the two new pieces are one more multiplicative factor and one more min() limit, so the human still sees a conviction-ranked size, just clamped for cross-cluster spread.
- Gate BOTH legs at approve: recompute cluster counts/dollars before the live Fidelity block (thematic_auto.py:5892) and block/shrink there too — the paper caps demonstrably do not gate the real order (it never reads cap_reason).
- Layer the caps as a ladder (finest first): per-theme count 3 (keep existing PORTFOLIO_MAX_PER_THEME) < per-cluster count ~4 & per-cluster $ 35% < GICS $ cap 30% (harden position_sizer.py:242 to fail-CLOSED as a secondary net) < per-position 10%. Count-caps stop many-small-names; $-caps stop few-large-names; they are complementary.
- Optional upstream soft tilt: add 'diversify across clusters; at most N names from the AI/semiconductor complex' to _build_ai_pick_prompt (thematic_auto.py:1633) and interleave clusters when truncating _merge_signals top-25 (:1376) so the LLM shortlist is pre-diversified — free, model-obeyed, pairs with the hard caps.
- Real holdings contribute to cluster weights via the GICS->macro fallback so a Fidelity book already heavy in ai_complex throttles new same-cluster paper/live picks (the current 30% sector cap only sees the paper book).

**Fit:** EXCELLENT fit for a HIL, propose-only, social-momentum $ book — better than risk-parity on every axis that matters here. (1) PROPOSE-ONLY: the book cannot autonomously sell to hit target weights, so classic drift-rebalancing is re-cast as pure entry-time gating (budget cap + tilt + count) — it only ever shrinks or withholds a PROPOSAL, never fires a trade, matching the system's 'none place orders autonomously' contract. (2) SOCIAL-MOMENTUM makes this necessary: buzz clusters by narrative, so when AI/semis trends the entire ranked[:25], the top-20 fed to the LLM, and all 6 picks are one macro bet — a per-name additive scorer has no way to notice; a cluster budget is the missing cross-section brake. (3) HIL EXPLAINABILITY: a cluster budget yields a one-line card reason ('ai_complex 34%/35% — capped' / 'trimmed size: cluster 80% full'), which a human can approve or override with `force=true`; an ERC covariance solve produces an opaque number the user cannot sanity-check. (4) ROBUST TO THIS PIPELINE's FLAKINESS: scrapers and yfinance .info are rate-limited and time out constantly; the cluster label rides the already-stored `theme` string (network-free), so the primary cap keeps biting when the covariance/sector data that ERC and the current GICS cap depend on has silently degraded to no-op. (5) SMALL-BOOK CORRECT: 10-20 names is too few for a stable covariance matrix but plenty for a count+dollar budget; MAX_NAMES_PER_CLUSTER≈4 on a 10-name book == ~40% count ceiling, coherent with a 35% dollar ceiling. (6) NON-DESTRUCTIVE to the edge: conviction×quality still fully sets the base size and the within-cluster ranking, so the system keeps 'concentration in the best ideas' — it just can't pile 100% of the book into one AI-supply-chain factor.

**Knobs:** THEMATIC_MAX_CLUSTER_PCT (default 35) — hard dollar budget per macro-cluster, as % of account; the primary cross-section spread ceiling., THEMATIC_MAX_NAMES_PER_CLUSTER (default 4) — pick-time COUNT backstop per cluster; consider expressing as a fraction of max_positions for book-size scaling., THEMATIC_DIV_FLOOR (default 0.30) — floor on the soft cluster_div_factor tilt multiplier (how hard a full cluster shrinks a new entry, never to zero)., THEMATIC_CLUSTER_MAP (default = built-in _THEME_MACRO) — env/JSON override of the theme->cluster fold so edge cases (nuclear, quantum) are user-tunable without code changes., THEMATIC_CLUSTER_CAP_ENABLED (default off->on) — master toggle for staged rollout (soft tilt first, then hard cap + count)., SIZER_MAX_SECTOR_PCT (existing, position_sizer.py:103, default 30) — keep the GICS $ cap as a secondary net; recommend hardening its fail-open at :242 to fail-CLOSED., PORTFOLIO_MAX_PER_THEME (existing, default 3) — keep as the finest within-cluster count cap beneath the new per-cluster count/budget., THEMATIC_CORRELATION_GUARD (existing, default off) + SIZER_CORR_THRESHOLD/SIZER_CORR_PENALTY_MAX — flip on / tune as the statistical backstop for when cluster labels disagree with actual price co-movement., THEMATIC_TARGET_CLUSTER_PCT (optional, default = MAX_CLUSTER_PCT) — decouple the soft-tilt anchor from the hard cap if you want the tilt to start biting before the budget ceiling.
